title: Surgical Technique and Photobiomodulation Therapy for Chronic Ankle Instability
official: A Prospective, Randomized, Comparative Clinical Trial on Surgical Technique and Photobiomodulation Therapy for Chronic Ankle Instability
summary:
The goal of this clinical trial is to understand the effects of modified Brostrom repair with suture tape augmentation (surgical treatment variable) and photobiomodulation therapy (rehabilitation variable) on the clinical outcomes of lateral ankle ligament repair to improve functional recovery and enhance return to duty / activity rates of active-duty service members and civilians alike, as applicable.

The main question it aims to answer is whether or not combining a modified Brostrom repair with suture tape augmentation with photobiomodulation therapy will enhance the clinical outcomes for lateral ankle ligament repair due to enhanced mechanical stability from suture tape augmentation, and reduced pain and inflammation, enhanced blood flow, and enhanced collagen production from photobiomodulation therapy.

Up to 300 male and female participants who are at least 18 years of age at screening who have been diagnosed with chronic ankle instability and meet all other eligibility requirements will be enrolled.
criteria:
Inclusion Criteria:

* Participant is willing and able to provide informed consent prior to Screening.
* Participant is ≥ 18 years of age at the time of screening.
* Diagnosed with Chronic Ankle Instability from any etiology
* Meets indications for LAL repair
* Willing to comply with the study protocol
* Active-Duty participants must obtain rehab care at the study-approved military facility

Exclusion Criteria:

* Participant is pregnant or has plans of becoming pregnant for the duration of the study.
* Participant with serious co-morbidities as determined by the Investigator.
* Active-Duty participants within one year of discharge (as they will not be able to meet follow-up requirements).
* Participants who are taking medications that have heat or light sensitive contraindications, such as but not limited to certain types of steroids.
* Participants with tattoos covering more than 30% of the area to be treated with PBMT.
* Participants with alcohol and drug abuse.
* Participants with connective tissue disorders.
* Participants with syndesmotic instability.
